title: Ethiopian Healing Barley Drink
community: All of Ethiopia — the restorative thin barley drink
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Atmit — a very thin, pourable barley or teff porridge-drink sweetened with honey and spiced with cinnamon, ginger, and cardamom. Ethiopia's restorative healing drink — given to the sick, to fasting individuals, and to those recovering from illness. More drink than food.
longDesc: See ETH014 for the full Atmit recipe and heritage. This is the drink version — thinner than the porridge version, served in a cup and drunk rather than eaten with a spoon.
ingredients: ½ cup roasted barley flour (or teff flour)
steps: Whisk barley flour into 1 cup cold water until smooth.
Bring remaining water to a simmer.
Cook 10—12 minutes, stirring, until very thin porridge consistency.
Remove from heat. Add honey, cinnamon, ginger, and cardamom.
Strain through a fine sieve for a completely smooth drink.
chefTips: Thinner than ETH014 (porridge version) — should pour freely.
commonMistakes: Too thick — should be a pourable drink.
servedWith: As a healing drink for the sick
culturalNote: Atmit drink is the care that Ethiopians give to each other — when someone is ill, atmit is prepared and brought to them. When someone is fasting and needs sustenance, atmit is available. It is nourishment as an act of love.
